method: Actual v59 inline game script and bot module executed together in an isolated JavaScript engine. Rendering, clock, DOM and Supabase transport are replaced by deterministic fixtures. No live match rows or highscores were read or written.

simulation.reference: v57 fixed automated reference opponent, including its legal placement rules, shot choices and reaction delay

tacticalOpponent.description: Same reference aiming and placement profile, additionally using the full 60-second balloon waiting strategy

checks: 60-second clock runs for bot and human; a timeout advances once
Repeated polls preserve the turn deadline
Impact animation locks input; old callbacks cannot skip a turn
Late placement responses cannot restore a previous result
Late highscore requests, timers and countdown frames are discarded
Selecting each bot level after GAME OVER starts a fresh match
Twelve consecutive bot rematches reset all match state
Online guest waits for host cleanup and never deletes placements
Duplicate rematch preparation is idempotent
Simultaneous rematch requests complete the handshake
Rematch still starts when a poll misses the short consent state
Castle events do not consume, replace or restart real projectiles
In-flight synchronization cannot alter the next round
Shared aim and launch match 544 physics samples on both sides for all weapons
Cancelled touch resets aiming without firing
Fullscreen cannot block starting; portrait fallback preserves touch coordinates
Initial START requests fullscreen inside the user gesture
Waiting uses visible balloons, bomb flight, both castle health values and remaining turn time
Easy, medium and hard have distinct time strategies; waiting stops for danger or deadline
Actual controller spends about 30 seconds waiting for its balloon to win before firing
Actual controller rechecks waiting and shoots when a new threat appears

limitations: Win rates describe these automated opponents, not a predicted probability against a particular human.
No physical iPhone, Safari rendering, native fullscreen or orientation permission was tested.
Online lifecycle fixtures mock transport responses; no live two-phone Supabase session was exercised.
The headless simulator runs deterministic 120 Hz projectile integration; idle simulation advances up to 250 ms and active animations at 60 fps.
